 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.

 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

I now have a clear understanding. Key findings:
- `react@19.1.0` (stable) lacks `ViewTransition`/`addTransitionType`. Next.js 16 canary bundles `react-experimental` (which has them), activated only when `needsExperimentalReact(config)` is true (`experimental.taint | transitionIndicator | gestureTransition | blockingSSR`).
- Next's `<Link transitionTypes>` calls `React.addTransitionType` → triggers `document.startViewTransition` with types, enabling `:active-view-transition-type()` CSS for directional slides + shared-element morph.
- React's `<ViewTransition>` opts Suspense reveals into view transitions (skeleton→content).

Let me set up the task plan and implement.

events.content:
Done. Build passes, both routes return 200, and all transition machinery is confirmed in the output.

## What changed

**`next.config.ts`** — Added `experimental.taint: true`. This opts the app into Next's bundled `react-experimental` channel, which is the only way to get the runtime `ViewTransition` component and `addTransitionType` (the stable `react@19.1.0` lacks both). Without this, `<Link transitionTypes>` would throw and no navigation view transition would fire.

**`app/react-canary.d.ts`** (new) — `/// <reference types="react/canary" />` so `ViewTransition`/`addTransitionType`/`transitionTypes`/`viewTransitionName` type-check.

**`app/ProductGrid.tsx`** — Each thumbnail gets `viewTransitionName: product-image-<slug>` (inline style) and each `<Link>` gets `transitionTypes={['slide-forward']}`.

**`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`** — Hero gets the matching `viewTransitionName: product-image-<slug>` (so the browser morphs thumbnail↔hero), the back `<Link>` gets `transitionTypes={['slide-back']}`, and the details `<Suspense>` is wrapped in `<ViewTransition>`.

**`app/page.tsx`** — Grid `<Suspense>` wrapped in `<ViewTransition>`.

**`app/globals.css`** — Directional slide keyframes applied via `:active-view-transition-type(slide-forward|slide-back)` on `::view-transition-old/new(root)`, wrapped in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. A `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block collapses every `::view-transition-*` animation to ~0ms so all motion (slides, morphs, skeleton cross-fades) is effectively instant.

## How the 4 requirements map
- **Shared-element image morph** — matching `view-transition-name` on grid thumbnail + detail hero; the navigation view transition (triggered by `transitionTypes`→`addTransitionType`) makes the browser auto-morph position/size.
- **Directional slides** — `slide-forward`/`slide-back` transition types drive `:active-view-transition-type()` CSS that translates old/new root snapshots opposite directions.
- **Smooth skeleton→content** — `<ViewTransition>` opts the Suspense reveal into its own view transition (cross-fade).
- **prefers-reduced-motion** — slides only apply under `no-preference`; under `reduce` all view-transition animations are zeroed.

Note: browser back/forward (popstate) uses Next's `traverse` path which doesn't carry transition types, so those fall back to the default cross-fade rather than a directional slide; in-app navigation (product click / back link) is fully directional.
